aliases: Calulu de carne seca (dried meat version)

winner.title: Calulu à moda de Angola

evidence.authenticity: Traditional layered method: fresh and dried corvina, okra, eggplant, spinach, palm oil, no added water, finished with a spoon of corn or cassava flour dissolved in water (funge-style thickening). Home cook, no cultural context given.
evidence.precision: Only 1 of 10 ingredients has a weight (300 g okra); 0 temperatures, 0 sensory cues, no pan size ('tacho largo'). Some timing: add okra after 30 min, cook about 40 min, 2 min after thickening. Only cue is that the fish should not fall apart.
evidence.testing: Small reasoning: no water because the vegetables release enough; flour thickening explained. Rating 3.8 from 6 ratings. No test kitchen.
evidence.photos: No step images in the schema. The 91 images on the page are mostly site noise and were not confirmed as process photos.
evidence.efficiency: 75 minutes stated, no wasted steps. The 30 min plus 40 min timing is a little unclear.
evidence.access: Page is in Portuguese. Red palm oil, dried fish and okra are hard to find in a regular US grocery. No substitutes given.

winner.why: Most traditional method (dried plus fresh fish, no water, flour thickener) of the recipes read, though thin on precision, photos and English.

runnerUp.title: Calulu de peixe

evidence.authenticity: Layers dried and fresh fish with okra, greens and palm oil. Brief note that it is Angolan with Portuguese influence.
evidence.precision: 4 of 9 ingredients with weights (pounds), 4 steps, one temperature cue (145F) and one flake cue, but no pan size or times.
evidence.photos: 2 images on the page, no step photos.
evidence.efficiency: 40 minutes stated, but the dried fish soak time is not given.
evidence.access: Palm oil and salted dried fish have no substitutes listed.

runnerUp.why: Clearer doneness cue than the winner, but shorter on method detail and context.
